title: 6. 10-Year Financial Forensics, Cash Conversion & Balance Sheet

epigraph.quote: Revenue is vanity, operating margin is sanity, and cumulative cash conversion over a full capex cycle is reality.
epigraph.author: Forensic Accounting Maxim

web_blocks.html: From FY15 through FY26 (and TTM Sep 2026), RPEL delivered one of the cleanest margin and return expansions in Indian specialty industrials [1]. Consolidated sales compounded from ₹38 Cr in FY15 to ₹257 Cr in FY26, reaching ₹315 Cr TTM [1]. Operating profit grew 25x over that span, jumping from ₹3 Cr (7% OPM) to ₹75 Cr (29% OPM) and ₹94 Cr TTM (30% OPM) [1]. Net profit climbed from ₹1 Cr in FY15 to ₹55 Cr in FY26 and ₹70 Cr TTM [1]. EPS rose from ₹0.26 to ₹11.94 (₹15.35 TTM), even after two 1:1 bonus issues took Equity Capital from ₹11 Cr (FY23) to ₹46 Cr (FY25–Sep 2026) [1].

web_blocks.caption: 10-Year + TTM Profit & Loss Statement (Consolidated from Mar 2021; Standalone Mar 2015–Mar 2020, ₹ Cr)
web_blocks.takeaway: Operating margins expanded structurally from 7% (FY15) to 29% (FY26) and 30% (TTM), driving a 42.2% 5-year profit CAGR with negligible interest cost.

web_blocks.caption: 10-Year + Sep 2026 Balance Sheet (₹ Cr)
web_blocks.takeaway: As of Sep 2026, Net Worth stands at ₹282 Cr against just ₹5 Cr of borrowings, with ₹25 Cr in Investments and ₹15 Cr in CWIP funding ongoing expansion.

web_blocks.caption: 10-Year Cash Flow Statement & CFO/EBITDA Conversion (₹ Cr)
web_blocks.takeaway: Cumulative FY21–FY26 CFO of ₹137 Cr covers cumulative capex and leaves positive FCF of ₹12 Cr (FY24), ₹25 Cr (FY25), and ₹23 Cr (FY26) despite heavy growth.

web_blocks.caption: 10-Year Working Capital & Return Ratios
web_blocks.takeaway: ROCE recovered to 30% in FY26 (30.3% current) and Debtor Days improved to 83, but Inventory Days (272) and CCC (255) remain elevated.

web_blocks.html: A cash-conversion audit across FY21–FY26 shows solid earnings quality tempered by inventory absorption [1]. Over those six years, RPEL earned cumulative PAT of ₹170 Cr (₹9 + ₹18 + ₹25 + ₹26 + ₹37 + ₹55 Cr) [1]. Cumulative Operating Cash Flow (CFO) reached ₹137 Cr (₹11 + ₹9 + ₹20 + ₹21 + ₹39 + ₹37 Cr), yielding an 80.6% PAT-to-CFO conversion rate [1]. On an EBITDA basis, CFO/EBITDA averaged ~75.5% across FY21–FY26 [1]. That ratio dipped from 86% in FY25 to 70% in FY26 only because inventory stocking absorbed cash during a 29% sales surge [1].

Quarterly momentum heading into FY27 was equally strong [1][23]. After posting ₹64 Cr in both Q2 FY26 and Q3 FY26, quarterly revenue climbed to ₹71 Cr in Q4 FY26 [1][23]. Sales then surged to ₹87 Cr in Q1 FY27 (+49% YoY) and ₹93 Cr in Q2 FY27 (+46% YoY) [1][23]. Through all four quarters from Dec 2025 to Sep 2026, quarterly OPM held flat at exactly 30% [1][23]. Steady 30% margins during rapid growth confirm that new export and domestic tonnage adds profit rather than diluting it [1].

web_blocks.title: Balance Sheet Fortress Ahead of the Odisha Capex Cycle
paragraphs: RPEL enters its ₹100 Cr Odisha JV (80% equity share) with almost zero debt [1][6]. Borrowings fell from ₹10 Cr (Mar 2023) to ₹5 Cr (Mar 2026 and Sep 2026), backed by ₹282 Cr of Equity + Reserves and ₹25 Cr of liquid Investments [1][6]. Annual CFO of ₹37–39 Cr lets RPEL self-fund its Odisha share without straining the balance sheet or diluting equity [1][6].

book_paragraphs: Now let's put on our forensic accountant's visor and read RPEL's ten-year financial statements from bottom to top. Over eleven years from FY15 to FY26, sales multiplied nearly sevenfold from ₹38 crore to ₹257 crore—and reached ₹315 crore on a trailing twelve-month basis through September 2026. Over that same span, operating profit grew twenty-five-fold from ₹3 crore to ₹75 crore, and ₹94 crore TTM. That gap between 7x revenue growth and 25x operating profit growth comes from one engine: operating margin expansion from 7% to 30%.

Equally important is how clean the balance sheet stayed while scaling. As of September 2026, RPEL carries ₹282 crore in equity and reserves against just ₹5 crore in borrowings, alongside ₹25 crore in investments. Even after two one-for-one bonus issues that took equity capital from ₹11 crore to ₹46 crore, earnings per share rose from ₹2.10 in FY21 to ₹11.94 in FY26 and ₹15.35 TTM. There is no debt-fueled financial engineering here.

book_subsections.title: Six-Year Cash Conversion & Quarterly Margin Consistency
paragraphs: Let's check the cash conversion math across the six consolidated years from FY21 through FY26. Total net profit across those six years sums to ₹170 crore. Total cash flow from operations sums to ₹137 crore—an 80.6% conversion of accounting profit into real operating cash. For a fast-growing manufacturing business that tripled its fixed assets over that period, 80.6% PAT-to-CFO conversion is respectable, and free cash flow stayed solidly positive at ₹12 crore in FY24, ₹25 crore in FY25, and ₹23 crore in FY26.

Why isn't cash conversion 100%? Because of the inventory line we flagged earlier. In FY26, CFO-to-EBITDA eased from 86% down to 70% as inventory days jumped to 272 days. Yet look at the quarterly P&L momentum through September 2026: sales stepped up from ₹64 crore in December 2025 to ₹71 crore in March, ₹87 crore in June, and ₹93 crore in September 2026, while operating margins held rock-steady at 30% in every single one of those four quarters.

The silver lining is that RPEL enters its ₹100 crore Odisha joint venture with TRL Krosaki from a position of pure balance-sheet strength—generating nearly ₹40 crore a year in operating cash with almost zero debt.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
book_callouts.text: 80.6% cumulative PAT-to-CFO conversion over a six-year period of 4x revenue growth confirms the earnings are real—and gives RPEL the cash firepower to self-fund its Odisha expansion.
